info.title: Velmora
info.description: The Velmora shop API for the mobile apps. JSON only. Errors are RFC 9457 application/problem+json with a stable `code`. Money is {amount_minor, currency, formatted}. Send Accept-Language: bn or en, and X-App-Platform / X-App-Version so an app that is too old can be told to update.

get.description: The policies a new customer must accept, with the release number to send back as `policy_releases` when registering or when a phone code creates the account. Empty when nothing has been published.

post.description: Makes a customer account and emails a verification link. Never returns a token: the person signs in afterwards. The answer is the same whether or not the address already has an account.
Customers only. An unknown account, a wrong password, a locked or disabled account and a staff account all get the same `auth.invalid_credentials`. Too many tries get 429 with Retry-After.
post.summary: Sign in with email or phone and password

post.description: Always answers 202 for a valid number, whether or not it has an account. `cooling_down` means a code was sent a moment ago and is still valid.
post.summary: Ask for a sign-in code by text message

post.description: A new number makes a new customer account, exactly as on the website. A wrong, expired or used code, a locked number and a staff number all get the same `auth.otp_invalid`.
post.summary: Sign in with a text-message code

post.description: Each refresh token works once. Using one a second time ends the whole sign-in (`auth.refresh_reused`), because it means a copy was stolen.
post.summary: Swap the refresh token for a new pair

post.description: Always answers 202, whether or not the address has an account.
post.summary: Ask for a password reset link

post.description: Every signed-in device is signed out. A used, expired or wrong token is a validation error on `token`.
post.summary: Set a new password with the emailed token

post.description: For people who have no password. The code goes to their verified phone.
post.summary: Send a code to confirm it is you

post.description: Send the password, or the code from /auth/reauth/code. For the next few minutes this sign-in may do sensitive things (change the password, later: email, phone, delete the account).

get.description: Active categories only, as a tree in the shop's own order (three levels deep at most in practice). A category under a hidden one is hidden too.
With its trail from the top (`ancestors`) and its direct sub-categories.
A hand-picked set of products (for example for a festival). The products themselves: `GET /products?filter[collection]=slug`.

Everything an app needs before it shows anything: languages, currency, how prices are shown, the oldest app version still served,
how to reach the shop, and the pages (policies, help) it can link to. Cached for a few minutes; send If-None-Match to ask cheaply.

post.description: Send it after every sign-in and whenever the push token changes. Registering the same token again updates it (200); a new one is created (201). Signing out removes the device.
post.summary: Register this phone for push messages

200.description: The device was already known and was updated.

delete.summary: Stop push messages to this phone

get.description: `division` is an id from `/geo/divisions`; an unknown one is 404.
`district` is an id from `/geo/districts`; an unknown one is 404.

post.description: Needs a recent confirmation (`auth.reauth_required` otherwise: call /auth/reauth first). Every other signed-in device is signed out; this one stays.

get.description: Published pages only. `body_html` is the shop's own sanitised HTML: show it in a web view or an HTML-capable text view. A page that exists only in another language, or only as a draft, is 404 (`page.not_found`). `GET /config` lists the pages and their slugs.

One scope at most: the whole shop, a category (with its sub-categories) or a collection. Narrow it with `filter[brand]`, `filter[type]`, `filter[in_stock]`, `filter[price_min]` / `filter[price_max]` (minor units, e.g. poisha) and `filter[attr][code]`. Sort by `newest`, `price_asc`, `price_desc` or `popular`. `meta.facets` tells which filters would leave something to show.

Everything the product page shows for one variant. Choose a variant by sending `options[code]=value` (for example `options[size]=m`); the answer says which values are selected, which would be in stock, the price of that variant and the `variant.id` to put in the cart. A slug from another language or an old spelling still finds the product; use the `slug` in the answer from then on.
Same category first, then same brand, then newest. Never the product itself.

`q` is 1 to 100 characters. Results come best first (`sort=relevance`, the default) or in any other order, and take the same `filter[...]`, `page` and `per_page` as the product list. When the exact words find nothing but a close spelling does, `meta.corrected_query` says which one was used. The first page of a real search is logged (text, language and result count only) to improve the shop.
Product names as someone types: at least 2 characters, at most 10 suggestions. Never logged and not personal, so it may be cached for a minute.

delete.description: `id` is the `id` from the list (also the `session_id` given at sign-in). Somebody else's, an ended one or an unknown one is 404.

http.description: The access_token from sign-in. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

current_password.description: People who signed up by phone have no password yet; for them the recent re-confirmation (a code) was the proof.

OtpVerifyRequest.description: The phone code, plus the device, plus (only needed when this first sign-in creates the account) the policies the person accepted.
OtpVerifyRequest.title: OtpVerifyRequest

ReauthRequest.description: Either the password or the code sent to the verified phone: exactly one.
ReauthRequest.title: ReauthRequest

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
